title: What If the Sun Became a Black Hole?
lines: What if the Sun suddenly became a black hole?
Here's what would happen. | The strangest part comes last.
For {8 minutes and 20 seconds~eight minutes and twenty seconds}, | nothing would change.
That's how long {sunlight/~sunlight} takes to reach us.
Even changes in gravity | only {travel/~travel} at the speed of {light./~light.}
Then, | the sky would go dark.
But Earth wouldn't fly off into space.
It would keep the same orbit, | {150 million kilometers~a hundred fifty million kilometers} out.
From that far, | a black hole {pulls/~pulls} like any star of the same mass.
Only mass and distance matter.
So how small is a black {hole/~hole} with the Sun's mass?
About {6 kilometers~six kilometers} wide. | Smaller than a city.
The whole Sun, | in a ball you {could/~could} drive across in minutes.
Back on Earth, | the cold {would/~would} set in fast.
Within weeks, | experts {estimate/~estimate} the land would {drop/~drop} below {−18 degrees~minus eighteen degrees}.
The oceans would freeze over from the top, | but under the ice, | the deep water could stay liquid for a very long {time./~time.}
But here's the twist: | the Sun can never do this.
It's far too light. | It would need to {be/~be} about {20 times~twenty times} heavier.
In about {5 billion years~five billion years}, | it will begin to {swell/~swell} into a red giant, | then {shrink/~shrink} to a white {dwarf/~dwarf} about the size of {Earth./~Earth.}
Crush Earth into a black hole instead. | How big would it be? | About the size of a marble, or about the size of a car? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: Crush the whole {Sun/~Sun} into a black hole, | and it would be just {6 kilometers~six kilometers} wide.
